_comment: Goes in the TARGET repo at .pi/models.json.
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. Until 2026-09-16 the pipeline sent no sampling
parameters at all. Pi only sends them when something defines them, and
OpenRouter does not substitute a default — it omits the parameter upstream
and whichever provider serves the request applies its own. `NOTES.md` 43.
TWO FIELDS, TWO JOBS.
`samplingParams` is merged verbatim into the request body, last, so its keys
beat pi's named fields (`models.md`, and openai-completions.js line 761).
It carries sampling and nothing else.
`compat.openRouterRouting` is sent AS-IS as the request's `provider` field
(openai-completions.js line 745). This is the native, typed home for
OpenRouter routing. We previously put the routing block inside
`samplingParams`, which also works — samplingParams is applied later and
wins — but routing is not sampling, and a reader will not look for it there.
ON `require_parameters: true`. It restricts routing to providers honouring
every parameter sent. Kept deliberately: if we pin sampling we want it
applied, and a provider quietly ignoring it is the silent failure this repo
keeps hitting. Checked against OpenRouter's /endpoints on 2026-09-16 rather
than assumed — every endpoint behind inkling and nemotron supports both
temperature and top_p, so the flag costs us no providers on those two.
exactly ONE endpoint, it does not support top_p, and sending it with
require_parameters on would have left zero eligible providers — a guaranteed
instant failure. It was latent only because the gatekeeper escalates on
authority without calling a model.
to google/gemma-4-26b-a4b-it:free. laguna had exactly ONE endpoint; when
Poolside rate-limited it the role was stuck for eight hours across three
attempts and `allow_fallbacks` had nowhere to fall back to (`NOTES.md` 48).
It also did not support `top_p`, which with require_parameters on would have
been zero eligible providers had the model ever been reached.
gemma-4-26b has ELEVEN endpoints and no low-bit quantization at all
(bf16/fp8/unknown), so it needs no `quantizations` filter. `scripts/pick-model.py`
ranked gemma-4-31b higher on redundancy alone (14 endpoints) but that one can
be served at fp4; for the role that holds merge rights, avoiding an unproven
quality risk is worth three endpoints. Both were defensible.
THE GATEKEEPER'S MODEL, 2026-09-17, second change in a day. laguna had one
endpoint and stayed rate-limited for eight hours; gemma-4-26b replaced it and
then hit Google's FREE-TIER INPUT CAP — 16,000 tokens per request for
`generate_content_free_tier_input_token_count`, which a prompt plus a diff
plus a role file exceeds every time. A BYOK key routed us to Google directly,
which was the right fix for the shared pool and no fix at all for the cap.
nemotron-3-super-120b is on Nvidia — the one provider we have same-day proof
is serving, because the implementer ran on it. Every free variant has exactly
one endpoint (`NOTES.md` 50), so provider choice is the only lever; picking
one that demonstrably works today beats picking an unknown one.
NOT SET YET, AND THE NEXT THING TO TRY: `quantizations`. The implementer's
model can be served at int4 (Darkbloom) and the gatekeeper's single endpoint
is fp4. That is `NOTES.md` 38's token soup with a name on it. Deliberately
NOT changed in the same pass that is meant to diagnose the reviewer — one
variable at a time. Note that laguna cannot be filtered at all: it has one
endpoint and any quantization filter leaves zero.
No `sort`. Sorting by throughput selects the fastest node, which is also how
you find a heavily quantised one.
